request.spec:
A steward can lock and unlock a period (buttons on the period; PERIOD_LOCKED and PERIOD_UNLOCKED
period=<name>; anyone else, or locking a locked period, is refused with an error on the period).
A locked period cannot be reopened. Show locked yes/no.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can lock and unlock a period (buttons on the period; PERIOD_LOCKED and PERIOD_UNLOCKED
period=<name>; anyone else, or locking a locked period, is refused with an error on the period).
A locked period cannot be reopened. Show locked yes/no.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Stewards can now lock and unlock a period, and a locked period can't be reopened. All 4 tests in the acceptance spec pass when run with `bin/e2e`.

- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V98__period_locked.sql`, adds a `locked` yes/no field to periods, defaulting to "no".
- **Server:**
  - **Who can lock:** only a user whose role is steward can lock or unlock. That includes someone a steward has delegated to, because the app already treats them as a steward. Anyone else is refused.
  - **What's refused:** locking a period that's already locked, unlocking one that isn't locked, and reopening a locked period. A refusal writes nothing to the store or the audit file.
  - **Audit:** a lock writes `PERIOD_LOCKED sheet=<id> by=<user> period=<name>` to the audit file, and an unlock writes the same line with `PERIOD_UNLOCKED`.
  - **Code:** the logic is in `PeriodService.lock(...)`, behind two new endpoints, `/lock` and `/unlock`, in `PeriodController`.
- **Front end:** each period row has a new "Locked" column showing yes or no (`period-locked`), plus Lock and Unlock buttons (`period-lock` and `period-unlock`). A refusal shows in the row's existing `period-error` element.

Two behaviours the request didn't specify:
- **Locking is separate from closing.** A steward can lock an open period, and a locked period can still be closed. Only reopening is blocked.
- **Copying a sheet doesn't keep the lock.** The existing copy already leaves out whether a period is closed, so I left out the lock as well.
